science.title: H6PD identified as a novel Parkinson's disease causal gene: disruption of ER-mitochondria interaction triggers neurodegeneration
science.description: While Parkinson’s disease (PD) involves complex factors, specific genetic causes often remain unknown. In Science Bulletin, a Central South University team identified H6PD as a novel PD causative gene, and found that H6PD mutations damage MAMs, the "bridges" between organelles. This "bridge failure" disables cleanup, causing mitochondrial buildup and neuron death. The study reveals a "H6PD-MAMs-Mitophagy" pathway, offering fresh targets for PD’s precision medicine.

science.title: Lightweight-efficient facial expression recognition with MSDE strategy for complex illumination
science.description: This paper presents a lightweight and efficient method designed for facial expression recognition (LEFER) under complex lighting conditions. Existing lightweight facial expression recognition methods have poor robustness when dealing with environmental changes, whereas methods with illumination invariance often face heavy computational burdens. LEFER integrates the multi-stage data enhancement (MSDE) strategy and the lightweight backbone network (LEFER-Net), which addresses this gap. The MSDE strategy combines geometric enhancement, photometric enhancement based on local Gaussian shadows, adaptive normalization, and the Mixup strategy to dynamically standardize input data, effectively addressing interferences such as spatial deformation, illumination fluctuations, and contrast attenuation. LEFER-Net involves three feature refinement stages and a classification head. First, the channel attention module based on local cross-channel interaction (LCCISCA) efficiently calibrates features. Second, the Gaussian mixture spatial attention (GMSA) module introduces a parameterized two-dimensional Gaussian kernel matrix to focus on key facial regions. Experimental results on FER-2013 and RAF-DB verify that LEFER achieves higher recognition accuracy while maintaining low parameter count and computational complexity. Ablation experiments and visualization results confirm that the proposed components effectively improve recognition accuracy under complex lighting conditions, achieving a favorable balance among recognition performance, illumination adaptability, and deployability.

science.title: Vericiguat mitigates inflammation and oxidative stress in lung tissue of rats with experimental asthma
science.description: Asthma is a chronic inflammatory airway disorder characterized by bronchial obstruction, airway hyperresponsiveness (AHR), and structural remodeling. Immune mediators, including interleukin‑6 (IL‑6), interleukin‑10 (IL‑10), interleukin‑17 (IL‑17), and tumor necrosis factor‑α (TNF‑α), together with oxidative stress, contribute to disease progression. Vericiguat, a soluble guanylate cyclase (sGC) stimulator acting through the nitric oxide–sGC–cyclic guanosine monophosphate (NO–sGC–cGMP) pathway, promotes smooth muscle relaxation and reduces hypertrophy, inflammation, and fibrosis. This study evaluated the antioxidant and anti‑inflammatory effects of vericiguat in an ovalbumin (OVA)‑induced asthma model in rats. Twenty‑five adult male Wistar rats were assigned to five groups: control, Asthma, dexamethasone 2.5 mg/kg, vericiguat 1 mg/kg, and vericiguat 0.5 mg/kg. Asthma was induced by OVA sensitization (intraperitoneal) followed by inhalation challenge. After induction, animals received treatments for seven days. Twenty‑four hours after the final dose, rats were euthanized, and lung tissues were collected. Left‑lung homogenates were analyzed for oxidative stress markers—glutathione peroxidase (GPX), superoxide dismutase (SOD), malondialdehyde (MDA), and total antioxidant capacity (TAC) as well as cytokines (TNF‑α, IL‑6, IL‑10, IL‑17) and nitric oxide (NO). Right‑lung samples were processed for hematoxylin and eosin (H&E) histopathology. OVA exposure increased TNF‑α, IL‑6, IL‑17, MDA, and NO while reducing GPX, SOD, TAC, and IL‑10. Vericiguat significantly reversed these alterations and reduced airway inflammation histologically. Vericiguat at both doses improved oxidative and inflammatory parameters in asthmatic rats, supporting its potential therapeutic relevance.

science.title: An explainable graph based inception framework for Aegle marmelos leaf disease classification
science.description: Aegle marmelos (bael) is a crucial medicinal tropical crop that has been largely overlooked in computational plant pathology studies. This study introduces AMnet, a cutting-edge deep learning framework that combines an InceptionV3 backbone with a fixed graph convolutional network. This integration effectively captures both within-region disease texture and between-region spatial propagation patterns, enabling the automated four-class classification of Aegle marmelos leaf diseases: Cercospora, healthy leaf, leaf curl, and leaf spot. The graph module constructs a 25-node spatial graph directly from the CNN feature maps, enabling end-to-end training without external preprocessing. Compared with MobileNetV2, InceptionV3, VGG19, and DenseNet201, AMnet demonstrated superior performance, achieving 98.83% accuracy, 98.84% F1-score, 99.95% PR-AUC, and 98.45% MCC, along with the fastest inference time of 1.83 ms. Its robustness was validated using bootstrap confidence interval estimation and four-fold cross-validation. PCA-based clustering analysis, supported by silhouette scoring and Davies–Bouldin indexing, confirmed clear class separability in the learned embeddings. Grad-CAM and LIME visualizations verified that the predictions were based on biologically significant leaf regions rather than background artifacts. A Gradio-based prototype demonstrated its practical deployment potential. Although broader field validation is still required, AMnet is an accurate, interpretable, and reproducible framework for diagnosing Aegle marmelos leaf disease.

science.title: Multimodal multitask deep learning for chili pepper disease diagnosis and severity estimation using images and agrometeorological data
science.description: Climate change is increasing the frequency of extreme weather events, profoundly altering the epidemiology of crop diseases, and threatening food security in vulnerable tropical agroecosystems. Although deep learning has revolutionized automated plant disease detection, prevailing models rely predominantly on unimodal visual analysis, often failing to capture the complex environmental interactions that govern pathogen development under field conditions. To overcome this limitation, we introduce a unified Multi-Task Learning (MTL) framework that simultaneously diagnoses disease type, localizes symptoms via pixel-level segmentation, and quantifies severity with high precision. Focusing on chili peppers (Capsicum annuum), we employ a curated dataset of 536 high-resolution field images (221 anthracnose, 196 TYLCV, 119 healthy); 527 images with complete climate linkage were retained and partitioned into training ($$N = 315$$), validation ($$N = 106$$), and independent test ($$N = 106$$) sets. To bolster symptom localization, 152 auxiliary anthracnose images were integrated exclusively for the segmentation branch, while a lesion-aware augmentation pipeline expanded the core multimodal training set to roughly 2,662 samples. The proposed end-to-end architecture is built upon a shared MobileNetV2 encoder. This backbone concurrently feeds a U-Net-style decoder, optimized using a novel Focal Tversky-based Hybrid Loss to address severe class imbalance caused by minute lesions, and a spatially aware multimodal fusion module. Within this module, global visual embeddings are concatenated with spatial summaries from the decoder and normalized climatic variables (temperature, humidity, rainfall, solar radiation, wind speed, and evapotranspiration) to inform subsequent dense layers. On the independent test set, the unified model achieved a classification accuracy of 99.06% (F1macro = 98.87%, MCC = 0.986), a leaf segmentation Dice of 0.844, and a disease-lesion Dice of 0.615, and a severity mean absolute error of 0.009 (global $$R^2 = 0.91$$). Specifically, an ablation study revealed that incorporating climatic variables and spatial fusion reduced severity estimation error by 25.6% compared to a baseline only for vision, confirming the vital role of environmental context. Integration of Explainable AI (SHAP) provided biological validation, autonomously identifying low solar radiation as a key driver of fungal infection and high radiation as a promoter of viral vectors. By effectively merging computer vision with agrometeorology in a lightweight architecture capable of real-time inference (92.5 ms), this research delivers a scalable, interpretable, and climate-resilient tool for next-generation precision agriculture.
